newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica 1996 results to boost shares.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica 1996 results to boost shares.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica de Espana reported an attractive set of 1996 results that will boost the telecommunication firm's shares after their recent slump, analysts said on Friday.
"Telefonica's results were slightly better than our expectations and illustrate that its value continues to be attractive," said an analyst at BBV Interactivos.

Telefonica gave details of its 1996 results on Friday after announcing the highlights at the end of January. The company reported a 20 percent increase in net profit to just over 160 billion pesetas ($1.1 billion).
The total dividend for 1996 rose 17 percent to 89 pesetas per share and cash flow per share rose to 863.50 compared with 798.70 in 1995.

"The dividend was slightly higher than our expectations and the operating cash flow level was also better than our forecasts, but not significantly," an analyst at BBV Interactivos said. He added that he expected the group's shares to rise to 3,800 pesetas by the end of the year.
In the days following the sale of the state's remaining 20.9 percent stake, Telefonica's shares slipped four percent to 3,240.

But in recent days, the shares have recovered some of their value, and by 1530 GMT, Telefonica shares were trading at 3,320, 10 pesetas higher than Thursday's close while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares stood 31.74 points down at 5,326.99.
Analysts welcomed the good quality of the company's full results on Friday.

In addition to a 16 percent increase in basic telephony income to 1,407.5 billion pesetas, the group reported a spectacular increase in its mobile telephone business that jumped 129 percent to 260 billion pesetas.
Its mobile customers grew 153 percent to 2.35 million.

Furthermore, the company highlighted its ability to contain costs, with its personnel costs rising just 2.0 percent while the parent company's workforce fell by 2,326 employees to 67,217 at the end of 1996.
Analysts said the group also took advantage of the fall in interest rates to reduce debt costs by 9.3 percent to 182.37 billion pesetas.
"The good sales, consumption, mobile telephone and cost restraint have managed to compensate for the negative extraordinary results," an analyst at Ibersecurities said.
The company reported that extraordinary costs had increased 16.6 percent due to payment and provisions for anticipated retirements.
According to a five-year strategic plan, the group is aiming to reduce its workforce by the year 2000 by 10,000 employees.
The international business results revealed no great surprises, analysts said.
The company said TISA's income, its subsidiary that manages its overseas units, grew 19 percent to 353.77 billion pesetas. This represented 15.2 percent of the group's total income.
Telefonica's chairman, Juan Villalonga, recently said the group's objective was to increase TISA's income to 20 percent of the total by the year 2000.
Villalonga on Friday invited the core shareholders -- Argentaria, BBV and La Caixa -- to increase their stakes in the group.
Each of the three core shareholders currently hold around five percent of Telefonica's capital.
"Speculation over an increase in these stakes could boost Telefonica's shares," an analyst at Credit Lyonnais said.
-- Madrid newsroom + 34 1 585 2196
($ = 143.5 Spanish Pesetas)
